### `shopping_mall_orders`

Customer purchase transactions capturing complete order state at the time
of purchase.

Orders represent the core commerce transaction entity, recording when a
customer completes a purchase. Each order has a unique order number for
reference, total price calculation, and a snapshot of the shipping
address to preserve delivery information even if the customer's address
changes later.

Orders belong to [shopping_mall_customers](#shopping_mall_customers) and contain multiple
[shopping_mall_order_items](#shopping_mall_order_items). Order status is derived from the
status of its order items rather than stored directly. Orders reference
product snapshots, variant snapshots, and seller profile snapshots
through their order items to maintain historical accuracy.

Soft delete support via deleted_at allows order hiding while preserving
transaction history for audit and customer records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer who placed this order. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `order_number`
  > Unique order number for customer reference and support lookup. Generated
  > sequentially or with timestamp prefix.
- `total_price`
  > Total order amount including all items, taxes, and shipping fees.
  > Captured at order time.
- `shipping_address_snapshot`
  > JSON snapshot of shipping address at order time containing
  > recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province,
  > postal_code, country. Preserves delivery address even if customer updates
  > their profile.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the order was placed.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the order was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the order was soft deleted (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_order_items`

Individual line items within customer orders representing purchased
product variants.

Each order item captures a specific product variant purchase with
quantity and unit price. The item maintains dual references: current
entities (product variant, seller) for operational purposes and
historical snapshots (product snapshot, product variant snapshot) for
order history integrity. This ensures order records remain accurate even
if products or variants change after purchase.

Order items follow a status workflow (PAID → SHIPPED → DELIVERED →
CANCELLED/REFUNDED) and serve as the foundation for downstream operations
including shipment assignment, cancellation requests, refund requests,
and review creation. Each item belongs to exactly one order and
references one product variant from one seller.

Related entities:
- [shopping_mall_orders](#shopping_mall_orders): Parent order containing this item
- [shopping_mall_product_variants](#shopping_mall_product_variants): Current product variant reference
- [shopping_mall_product_snapshots](#shopping_mall_product_snapshots): Historical product state at
order time
- [shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots](#shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots): Historical variant
state at order time
- [shopping_mall_sellers](#shopping_mall_sellers): Current seller reference
- [shopping_mall_shipment_items](#shopping_mall_shipment_items): Shipment assignments for this item
- [shopping_mall_cancellation_requests](#shopping_mall_cancellation_requests): Cancellation requests for
this item
- [shopping_mall_refund_requests](#shopping_mall_refund_requests): Refund requests for this item
- [shopping_mall_reviews](#shopping_mall_reviews): Customer reviews linked to this item

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`: Parent order's [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders) containing this line item.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`
  > Current product variant's [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants) for
  > operational reference.
- `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id`
  > Product snapshot's [shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id](#shopping_mall_product_snapshots) capturing
  > historical product state at order time.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id`
  > Product variant snapshot's {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id} capturing historical variant
  > state at order time.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`: Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers) who listed this product variant.
- `quantity`: Number of units purchased in this line item.
- `unit_price`: Price per unit at order time, preserved for historical accuracy.
- `status`
  > Current fulfillment status: PAID (payment confirmed), SHIPPED (sent to
  > customer), DELIVERED (received by customer), CANCELLED (order cancelled
  > before shipment), or REFUNDED (refund processed after delivery).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this order item was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this order item was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this order item was soft-deleted, null if active.

### `shopping_mall_shipments`

Shipments created by sellers to track order item deliveries with carrier
information and delivery lifecycle timestamps.

Represents the physical shipment of order items from a seller to a
customer. Each shipment contains tracking information including carrier
name and tracking number, along with timestamps marking key delivery
milestones: when the shipment was sent (shipped_at), when it was
delivered (delivered_at), when the customer confirmed receipt
(delivery_confirmed_at), and the automatic delivery confirmation
timestamp (auto_delivered_at).

Shipments are created by sellers after order items are paid and ready to
ship. Multiple shipments can exist for a single order when items come
from different sellers. The [shopping_mall_shipment_items](#shopping_mall_shipment_items) table
links individual order items to their corresponding shipments.

Delivery lifecycle:
- shipped_at: When seller hands package to carrier
- delivered_at: When carrier marks package as delivered
- delivery_confirmed_at: When customer manually confirms receipt
- auto_delivered_at: System-calculated auto-confirmation (shipped_at + 14
days)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`: Belonged order's [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `tracking_carrier`
  > Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL, USPS). Null until
  > shipment is created.
- `tracking_number`
  > Tracking number provided by the carrier for package tracking. Null until
  > shipment is created.
- `shipped_at`
  > Timestamp when the seller handed the package to the carrier. Null until
  > actually shipped.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when the carrier marked the package as delivered. Null until
  > delivery occurs.
- `delivery_confirmed_at`
  > Timestamp when the customer manually confirmed receipt of the shipment.
  > Null if not confirmed.
- `auto_delivered_at`
  > System-calculated timestamp for automatic delivery confirmation
  > (shipped_at + 14 days). Used when customer doesn't manually confirm.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the shipment record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the shipment record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the shipment was soft deleted. Null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_items`

Junction table linking shipments to order items, enabling one shipment to
contain multiple order items from the same seller. Each order item
belongs to exactly one shipment, tracked through the unique constraint on
order_item_id. This table supports consolidated shipment tracking where
sellers ship multiple order items together with unified tracking
information.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shipment_id`: Belonged shipment's [shopping_mall_shipments.id](#shopping_mall_shipments).
- `order_item_id`: Belonged order item's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items).
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for record removal tracking.

### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Customer reviews and ratings for purchased products with verified order
item linkage. Each review represents authentic feedback from a customer
who has purchased and received a specific product. Reviews are linked to
order items to verify purchase authenticity and enforce
one-review-per-order constraint. Supports soft deletion to preserve
review history while hiding content from public view. Related to {@link
shopping_mall_review_snapshots} which preserves immutable historical
states of review edits.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`: Customer who wrote the review. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers)
- `shopping_product_id`: Product being reviewed. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products)
- `shopping_order_item_id`
  > Order item that verified this purchase. Ensures review is from actual
  > buyer. [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items)
- `rating`: Product rating from 1 to 5 stars.
- `content`: Optional review content with detailed feedback and comments.
- `deleted`
  > Soft delete flag. When true, review is hidden from public view but
  > preserved in database.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the review was first created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the review was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the review was soft deleted. Null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_review_snapshots`

Immutable historical snapshots of review state changes.

Captures point-in-time states of reviews whenever they are edited or
deleted, preserving the rating and content as they existed at that
moment. These snapshots serve critical business purposes:

- **Audit trail**: Complete history of review modifications for transparency
- **Dispute resolution**: Evidence of review content at any point in time
- **Post-deletion access**: Reviews remain accessible through snapshots
even after soft deletion
- **Historical display**: Shows what review looked like when order was
evaluated

Each snapshot is created automatically before a review update or delete
operation. Once created, snapshots are never modified or deleted,
ensuring data integrity for compliance and dispute resolution scenarios.

Related to [shopping_mall_reviews](#shopping_mall_reviews) through shopping_mall_review_id
foreign key. Multiple snapshots can exist for a single review, forming a
chronological history.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`
  > Parent review's [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews). Establishes which
  > review this snapshot captures the state of.
- `snapshot_by_user_id`
  > Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers) who triggered this snapshot
  > creation through edit or delete operation. Provides audit trail of who
  > made the change.
- `rating`
  > Review rating at snapshot time. Integer value from 1 to 5 stars.
  > Denormalized from parent review to preserve historical state.
- `content`
  > Review text content at snapshot time. Optional detailed feedback from
  > customer. Denormalized from parent review to preserve historical state,
  > including null values if review had no content.
- `snapshot_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the exact moment the
  > review state was captured, typically just before an update or delete
  > operation.
- `created_at`
  > Database record creation timestamp. Automatically set when snapshot row
  > is inserted.

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`

Customer cancellation requests for order items with status workflow and
seller response tracking.

Represents formal requests submitted by customers to cancel specific
order items before or after shipment. Each request captures the
cancellation reason, current status (PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED), and
tracks the seller's response when applicable.

Key relationships:
- [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items): The order item being cancelled
(required, 1:N relationship)
- [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers): The customer who submitted the
request (required)
- [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers): The seller who responded to the
request (nullable, only for APPROVED/REJECTED status)

Behavioral notes:
- Status workflow: PENDING → APPROVED or REJECTED
- Only order items with PAID status can be cancelled (business rule)
- responded_at and responded_by_seller_id are null when status is PENDING
- Immutable history preserved in {@link
shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots}

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`: Target order item's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items) being cancelled.
- `customer_id`: Submitted customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `responded_by_seller_id`
  > Responding seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers). Null when status is
  > PENDING.
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting cancellation.
- `status`: Current cancellation status: PENDING, APPROVED, or REJECTED.
- `requested_at`: Timestamp when the customer submitted the cancellation request.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when the seller responded to the request. Null when status is
  > PENDING.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null when record is active.

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of cancellation request states for audit trail and
dispute resolution.

Captures point-in-time states whenever a cancellation request's status
changes or is responded to by the seller. Each snapshot preserves the
complete state including reason, status, and response details at the
moment of capture. Snapshots are append-only and never modified or
deleted, ensuring a complete historical record for dispute resolution and
compliance auditing.

Related to [shopping_mall_cancellation_requests](#shopping_mall_cancellation_requests) as the parent
entity. Multiple snapshots can exist for a single cancellation request,
creating a chronological audit trail of all state changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `cancellation_request_id`
  > Parent cancellation request's {@link
  > shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.
- `responded_by_seller_id`
  > Seller who responded to the cancellation request's {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}. Null if no response yet.
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting cancellation, captured at snapshot time.
- `status`
  > Cancellation request status at snapshot time. Valid values: PENDING,
  > APPROVED, REJECTED.
- `requested_at`
  > Original timestamp when the cancellation request was submitted by the
  > customer.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when the seller responded to the cancellation request. Null if
  > no response yet.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

### `shopping_mall_refund_requests`

Customer refund requests for order items with delivery date tracking for
7-day validation.

Represents refund requests submitted by customers for delivered order
items. Each request tracks the reason for refund, current status
(PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED), and delivery date to validate the 7-day
refund window. Sellers respond to requests by updating status and
recording response timestamp.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to [shopping_mall_order_items](#shopping_mall_order_items) - the specific order item
being refunded
- Submitted by [shopping_mall_customers](#shopping_mall_customers) - the customer requesting
refund
- Responded by [shopping_mall_sellers](#shopping_mall_sellers) - the seller who processes
the request (nullable until responded)
- Has immutable snapshots in {@link
shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots} for audit trail

Business constraints:
- Refund requests only allowed within 7 days of delivery (validated by
delivered_at)
- Status transitions: PENDING → APPROVED or PENDING → REJECTED
- One refund request per order item (enforced by unique index on
order_item_id)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`
  > Order item's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items). The specific order
  > item being refunded.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers) who submitted the refund
  > request.
- `responded_by_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers) who responded to the refund
  > request. Null until seller responds.
- `reason`
  > Customer's reason for requesting refund. Explains why the customer wants
  > a refund for this order item.
- `status`
  > Current status of the refund request. Values: PENDING (awaiting seller
  > response), APPROVED (seller approved refund), REJECTED (seller rejected
  > refund).
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when the order item was delivered. Used to validate the 7-day
  > refund request window.
- `requested_at`: Timestamp when the customer submitted the refund request.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when the seller responded to the refund request. Null until
  > seller responds.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the refund request record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the refund request record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the refund request was soft deleted. Null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of refund request states for audit trail and dispute
resolution.

Captures point-in-time states of refund requests including all business
fields and relationships at the moment of state change. These snapshots
preserve the complete refund request context (order item, customer,
seller response) whenever status transitions occur (submission, approval,
rejection).

Referenced by [shopping_mall_refund_requests](#shopping_mall_refund_requests) for historical audit
access. Used in dispute resolution to verify the timeline of refund
request processing, validate 7-day delivery windows, and ensure
compliance with platform refund policies. Append-only table - never
updated or deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `refund_request_id`
  > Parent refund request's [shopping_mall_refund_requests.id](#shopping_mall_refund_requests).
  > Establishes the audit trail relationship.
- `order_item_id`
  > Order item's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items) that this refund
  > request concerns. Captured at snapshot time for historical accuracy.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers) who submitted the refund
  > request. Captured at snapshot time for historical accuracy.
- `responded_by_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers) who responded to the refund
  > request. Null if pending or auto-processed.
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting the refund at the time of snapshot.
- `status`
  > Refund request status at snapshot time. Values: PENDING, APPROVED,
  > REJECTED.
- `delivered_at`
  > Delivery confirmation timestamp for 7-day refund validation window. Null
  > if not yet delivered at snapshot time.
- `requested_at`
  > Timestamp when the refund request was originally submitted. Captured for
  > historical accuracy.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when seller responded to the refund request. Null if pending at
  > snapshot time.
- `snapshot_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, capturing the point-in-time
  > state.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit purposes.

elevation and tracks the review workflow through status transitions

to requests, with response metadata recorded for audit purposes. Related
to [shopping_mall_admin_request_snapshots](#shopping_mall_admin_request_snapshots) which preserve immutable

and response details. Snapshots are created when requests are submitted

never modified or deleted, ensuring complete audit history for platform
governance and compliance.

instruction:
## API Interface Requirements

### Authentication & Account Management

**Customer Authentication**
- POST /auth/customer/signup - Customer registration with email and password
- POST /auth/customer/login - Customer login with email and password
- POST /auth/customer/logout - Customer logout
- POST /auth/customer/password/change - Change password (requires current password)
- DELETE /auth/customer/account - Delete customer account (preserves orders and reviews)

**Seller Authentication**
- POST /auth/seller/signup - Seller registration with email and password
- POST /auth/seller/login - Seller login with email and password
- POST /auth/seller/logout - Seller logout
- POST /auth/seller/password/change - Change password
- GET /auth/seller/approval-status - View approval status (pending, approved, rejected with reason)
- POST /auth/seller/reregister - Submit new registration after rejection
- DELETE /auth/seller/account - Delete seller account (validates no pending orders/requests)

### Customer Profile
- GET /customers/profile - Get current customer's profile
- PUT /customers/profile - Update display name and phone number

### Address Management
- GET /customers/addresses - List all addresses for current customer
- POST /customers/addresses - Add new shipping address
- PUT /customers/addresses/:id - Edit address
- DELETE /customers/addresses/:id - Delete address
- POST /customers/addresses/:id/set-default - Set address as default

### Seller Profile
- GET /sellers/profile - Get current seller's profile
- PUT /sellers/profile - Update shop name, description, logo (creates snapshot)
- GET /sellers/profile/:id - View any seller's profile (public)
- GET /sellers/profile/:id/snapshots - View seller's profile snapshots (owner/admin only)

### Categories
- GET /categories - List all categories (with subcategories)
- GET /categories/:id/products - View products in a category
- POST /admin/categories - Create category/subcategory (admin only)
- PUT /admin/categories/:id - Edit category (admin only)
- DELETE /admin/categories/:id - Delete category (admin only)

### Products
- GET /products - Search products (paginated, with filters: category, price range, in-stock, sort options)
- GET /products/:id - View product detail (all images, variants, seller info, reviews, ratings)
- POST /sellers/products - Create product (seller only)
- PUT /sellers/products/:id - Edit product (creates snapshot, seller only)
- DELETE /sellers/products/:id - Delete product (validates no pending orders/requests, seller only)
- GET /sellers/products/:id/snapshots - View product snapshots (seller/admin)
- GET /admin/products - List all products (admin only)
- DELETE /admin/products/:id - Delete any product (admin only)

### Product Images
- POST /sellers/products/:productId/images - Upload product image
- PUT /sellers/products/:productId/images/reorder - Reorder images (set display order)
- DELETE /sellers/products/:productId/images/:imageId - Delete image

### Product Variants (SKU)
- POST /sellers/products/:productId/variants - Add variant to product
- PUT /sellers/products/:productId/variants/:variantId - Edit variant (creates snapshot)
- DELETE /sellers/products/:productId/variants/:variantId - Delete variant (validates no pending orders/requests)

### Inventory Management
- GET /sellers/variants/:variantId/inventory - View inventory history for variant
- POST /sellers/variants/:variantId/inventory - Add inventory record (restock/adjustment with quantity and reason)

### Wishlist
- GET /customers/wishlist - View customer's wishlist (paginated)
- POST /customers/wishlist/products/:productId - Add product to wishlist
- DELETE /customers/wishlist/products/:productId - Remove product from wishlist

### Shopping Cart
- GET /customers/cart - View cart with all items and total
- POST /customers/cart/items - Add variant to cart (combines quantities if same variant exists)
- PUT /customers/cart/items/:itemId - Update item quantity
- DELETE /customers/cart/items/:itemId - Remove item from cart

### Checkout & Orders
- GET /customers/checkout/review - Review order summary before placement
- POST /customers/checkout - Place order (creates order, decreases stock, clears cart items)
- GET /customers/orders - View order history (paginated, sorted by newest)
- GET /customers/orders/:id - View order detail (items, shipments, tracking)

### Order Management
- GET /sellers/orders - View order items for seller's products (filterable by status)
- GET /admin/orders - View all orders (admin only)

### Shipping & Tracking
- POST /sellers/shipments - Create shipment with items and tracking info
- GET /customers/shipments/:id - View shipment tracking
- POST /customers/shipments/:id/confirm-delivery - Confirm delivery for shipment

### Cancellation Requests
- POST /customers/order-items/:itemId/cancellation - Request cancellation for order item (PAID status only)
- GET /sellers/cancellation-requests - View pending cancellation requests for seller's items
- POST /sellers/cancellation-requests/:id/approve - Approve cancellation request
- POST /sellers/cancellation-requests/:id/reject - Reject cancellation request
- GET /sellers/cancellation-requests/:id/snapshots - View cancellation request snapshots
- POST /admin/order-items/:itemId/cancel - Force cancel order item (admin only)

### Refund Requests
- POST /customers/order-items/:itemId/refund - Request refund for order item (DELIVERED status, within 7 days)
- GET /sellers/refund-requests - View pending refund requests for seller's items
- POST /sellers/refund-requests/:id/approve - Approve refund request
- POST /sellers/refund-requests/:id/reject - Reject refund request
- GET /sellers/refund-requests/:id/snapshots - View refund request snapshots
- POST /admin/order-items/:itemId/refund - Force refund order item (admin only)

### Reviews & Ratings
- POST /customers/order-items/:itemId/review - Create review for delivered item (one per product per order)
- PUT /customers/reviews/:id - Edit review (creates snapshot)
- DELETE /customers/reviews/:id - Delete review (soft delete, snapshots preserved)
- GET /products/:id/reviews - View all reviews for product (paginated, sorted by newest)

### Seller Dashboard
- GET /sellers/dashboard - View shop summary (product count, order items count, pending cancellation/refund counts)

### Administrator System
- POST /admin/promotion-requests - Submit request to become administrator
- GET /admin/promotion-requests - View pending promotion requests (super admin only)
- POST /admin/promotion-requests/:id/approve - Approve promotion request (super admin only)
- POST /admin/promotion-requests/:id/reject - Reject promotion request (super admin only)
- POST /admin/users/:userId/promote - Promote admin to super admin (super admin only)
- POST /admin/users/:userId/demote - Demote super admin to regular admin (super admin only, cannot demote self)

### Seller Management (Admin)
- GET /admin/sellers/pending - View pending seller approvals
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/approve - Approve seller registration
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/reject - Reject seller registration (with reason)
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/suspend - Suspend seller account
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/unsuspend - Unsuspend seller account
- GET /admin/sellers - View all seller accounts

### User Management (Admin)
- GET /admin/customers - View all customer accounts
- POST /admin/customers/:id/ban - Ban customer account
- POST /admin/customers/:id/unban - Unban customer account
- GET /admin/sellers - View all seller accounts
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/ban - Ban seller account
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/unban - Unban seller account

### Request/Response DTOs

**Authentication**
- Signup: { email, password }
- Login: { email, password }
- Password change: { currentPassword, newPassword }

**Customer Profile**
- Profile: { displayName, phoneNumber }
- Profile update: { displayName?, phoneNumber? }

**Address**
- Address create/update: { recipientName, phoneNumber, streetAddress, city, stateProvince, postalCode, country, isDefault? }

**Seller Profile**
- Seller profile: { shopName, shopDescription, logoImageUrl }
- Seller profile update: { shopName?, shopDescription?, logoImageUrl? }

**Category**
- Category: { id, name, description, parentCategoryId?, subcategories?[] }
- Category create/update: { name, description, parentCategoryId? }

**Product**
- Product: { id, sellerId, categoryId, name, description, basePrice, images[], variants[], seller: { shopName }, averageRating, reviewCount }
- Product create: { name, description, categoryId, basePrice }
- Product update: { name?, description?, categoryId?, basePrice? }

**Product Image**
- Image: { id, imageUrl, displayOrder }
- Image reorder: { imageIds: string[] } (ordered array)

**Product Variant**
- Variant: { id, skuCode, optionValues: { [key: string]: string }, price?, stockQuantity }
- Variant create: { skuCode, optionValues, price?, stockQuantity }
- Variant update: { skuCode?, optionValues?, price?, stockQuantity? }

**Inventory**
- Inventory record: { id, quantityChange, reason, createdAt }
- Inventory add: { quantityChange, reason: "RESTOCK" | "ADJUSTMENT" | "ORDER" | "CANCELLATION" | "REFUND" }

**Wishlist**
- Wishlist item: { id, product: { id, name, basePrice, mainImage }, addedAt }

**Cart**
- Cart: { items: CartItem[], totalPrice }
- Cart item: { id, product: { name }, variant: { optionValues }, price, quantity, subtotal, available, stockWarning }
- Cart add: { variantId, quantity }
- Cart update: { quantity }

**Checkout**
- Checkout review: { items: OrderItemPreview[], shippingAddress, totalPrice }
- Checkout: { addressId }

**Order**
- Order: { id, orderNumber, createdAt, totalPrice, status, items: OrderItem[], shippingAddress, shipments[] }
- Order item: { id, product: { name }, variant: { optionValues }, quantity, unitPrice, status, seller: { shopName } }
- Order summary (list): { id, orderNumber, createdAt, totalPrice, status }

**Shipment**
- Shipment: { id, orderItems: [], trackingCarrier, trackingNumber, shippedAt, deliveredAt?, deliveryConfirmedAt? }
- Shipment create: { orderItemIds: string[], trackingCarrier, trackingNumber }

**Cancellation/Refund Request**
- Request: { id, orderItemId, reason, status, requestedAt, respondedAt? }
- Request create: { reason }
- Request approve/reject: { } (empty body, status in URL)

**Review**
- Review: { id, rating, content?, createdAt, updatedAt, user: { displayName } }
- Review create: { rating, content? }
- Review update: { rating?, content? }

**Seller Dashboard**
- Dashboard: { productCount, orderItemCount, pendingCancellationCount, pendingRefundCount }

**Admin Promotion**
- Promotion request: { id, user: { email, currentRole }, reason, status, requestedAt }
- Promotion request create: { reason }

**Pagination**
- All list endpoints support: ?page=1&limit=20&sort=createdAt,desc

**Filtering**
- Product search: ?categoryId=&minPrice=&maxPrice=&inStock=&sort=newest|priceAsc|priceDesc
- Seller orders: ?status=PAID|SHIPPED|DELIVERED|CANCELLED|REFUNDED

operations.specification: Handles customer registration by creating a new customer account with email and password. The service validates email uniqueness against the shopping_mall_customers table, hashes the password using bcrypt, and creates the customer record. Upon successful registration, generates JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer). Returns the authorized customer information including tokens for immediate authentication.
operations.description:
Registers a new customer account with email and password credentials.

This endpoint creates a new customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table with the provided email address and bcrypt-hashed password. The email must be unique across all customer accounts. Upon successful registration, the system automatically authenticates the customer by generating JWT access and refresh tokens.

The registration process includes creating a session record in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table to track the login session with connection metadata including IP address, initial page URL, and referrer. This enables security auditing and session management.

The response includes the customer's authorized status with access token, refresh token, and expiration information. The customer can immediately use these tokens to access protected endpoints requiring customer authentication.

Related operations include POST /auth/customer/login for existing customers and POST /auth/customer/refresh for token renewal.

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized customer information with JWT tokens.

operations.specification: Authenticates customer credentials by validating email and password against the shopping_mall_customers table. The service retrieves the customer record by email, verifies the bcrypt password hash, checks that the account is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null), and generates JWT access and refresh tokens. Creates a new session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with connection metadata. Returns authorized customer information with tokens.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer with email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates the provided email and password against the shopping_mall_customers table. The service retrieves the customer record by email address and verifies the bcrypt-hashed password. The authentication fails if the email does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the account has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null).

Upon successful authentication, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a new session record in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. The session includes connection metadata such as IP address, initial page URL, and referrer for security auditing purposes.

The response contains the authorized customer information including the access token, refresh token, and expiration timestamp. Customers use these tokens to access protected endpoints requiring customer authentication.

Related operations include POST /auth/customer/join for new registration and POST /auth/customer/refresh for token renewal without re-authentication.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized customer information with JWT tokens.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refreshes JWT access token using a valid refresh token. The service validates the refresh token against active sessions in shopping_mall_customer_sessions, checks the session has not expired (expired_at), verifies the associated customer account exists and is not soft deleted, then generates new access and refresh tokens. Creates a new session record for token rotation. Returns updated authorized customer information with new tokens.
operations.description:
Refreshes JWT access token using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint enables customers to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating with credentials. The service validates the provided refresh token against active sessions in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, ensuring the session has not expired based on the expired_at timestamp.

The refresh operation also verifies that the associated customer account still exists and has not been soft deleted (deleted_at is null). If the customer account has been deleted or suspended, the refresh request is rejected.

Upon successful validation, the system generates new access and refresh tokens and creates a new session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions for token rotation. This approach maintains security by limiting token lifetime while providing seamless authentication continuity.

The response includes the updated authorized customer information with new access token, refresh token, and expiration timestamp. This operation is essential for maintaining long-lived user sessions without requiring repeated credential entry.

Related operations include POST /auth/customer/login for initial authentication and POST /auth/customer/join for new customer registration.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized customer information with refreshed JWT tokens.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Service layer creates seller account transactionally: (1) Validate email uniqueness across sellers and admins, (2) Hash password using bcrypt, (3) Create shopping_mall_sellers record with approval_status='PENDING', (4) Create email verification token in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications, (5) Generate JWT access and refresh tokens, (6) Create session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions with IP/href/referrer metadata, (7) Return IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized with tokens and seller info. Transaction rolls back on any failure. Email verification is sent asynchronously.
operations.description:
Register a new seller account with email, password, and shop information.

This endpoint creates a new seller account in the shopping mall platform. The seller registration requires email, password, and basic shop information including shop name and description. Upon successful registration, the seller account is created with approval_status set to 'PENDING', requiring administrator review before the seller can list products and manage inventory.

The registration process stores the seller's credentials securely with bcrypt password hashing. An email verification token is automatically generated and sent to the provided email address through the shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table. The seller must verify their email before the account becomes fully active, though admin approval is still required separately.

Authentication considerations include email uniqueness validation against existing sellers and admins, password strength requirements, and prevention of duplicate shop names. The response includes JWT access and refresh tokens, allowing immediate authenticated access, though certain seller operations remain restricted until admin approval is granted.

Related operations include POST /auth/seller/login for returning sellers, and sellers can check their approval status through the dashboard or profile endpoints after registration.

requestBody.description: Seller registration information including credentials and shop details.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller account information for newly registered seller.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service layer authentication flow: (1) Query shopping_mall_sellers by email, (2) Verify account not deleted (deleted_at is null), (3) Compare password using bcrypt against password_hash, (4) Check account not suspended, (5) Generate JWT access token (short-lived) and refresh token (long-lived), (6) Create session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions with ip, href, referrer, expired_at, (7) Return IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized with tokens, seller id, email, shop_name, approval_status. Failed authentication returns 401 without revealing whether email or password was incorrect.
operations.description:
Authenticate seller with email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates seller credentials and establishes an authenticated session. The seller provides their registered email address and password, which are verified against the shopping_mall_sellers table. Upon successful authentication, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens for subsequent API requests.

The login process performs several validation checks: verifying the email exists in the sellers table, comparing the provided password against the stored bcrypt password_hash, checking that the account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), and validating the account is not suspended. Note that sellers with approval_status='PENDING' or 'REJECTED' can still login to check their status, but cannot perform seller operations requiring approval.

Session tracking is implemented through the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table, which records each login with connection metadata including IP address, request URL (href), and referrer. This creates an audit trail for security monitoring. The session record includes an expiration timestamp (expired_at) that enforces session lifetime limits.

The response contains JWT tokens in the IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized format. The access token is used for authenticating subsequent API requests, while the refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication. Related operations include POST /auth/seller/join for new registration and POST /auth/seller/refresh for token renewal.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller account information for authenticated seller.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Service layer token refresh: (1) Extract refresh token from request body, (2) Query shopping_mall_seller_sessions to find matching session (token stored or derived), (3) Verify session not expired (expired_at > now), (4) Verify seller account exists and not deleted/suspended, (5) Generate new JWT access token with updated claims, (6) Optionally generate new refresh token and update session, (7) Return IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized with new tokens. Invalid or expired tokens return 401. Session cleanup removes expired sessions periodically.
operations.description:
Refresh JWT access token using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint enables sellers to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating with credentials. When the short-lived access token expires, the seller can present their refresh token to this endpoint to receive a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token through token rotation).

The refresh token validation process verifies the token against active sessions in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. The system checks that the session has not expired (expired_at is in the future), the seller account still exists and is not soft-deleted, and the account has not been suspended since the session was created. If any of these conditions fail, the refresh request is rejected and the seller must re-authenticate.

Token rotation can be implemented for enhanced security: each refresh operation invalidates the old refresh token and issues a new one. This limits the window of opportunity if a refresh token is compromised. The session record is updated with new expiration timestamps during the refresh operation.

This endpoint requires no authentication decorator since it operates on the refresh token itself rather than an access token. The refresh token is typically sent in the request body or as a secure HTTP-only cookie. Related operations include POST /auth/seller/login for initial authentication and the general pattern of including access tokens in Authorization headers for protected endpoints.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access token.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens for continued seller session.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Create a new administrator account with email and password. Validates email uniqueness across all administrator accounts. Stores bcrypt-hashed password securely. Sets initial grade to ADMIN (super admin assignment requires promotion by existing super admin). Creates the administrator record in shopping_mall_admins table with generated UUID. Returns JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication. Email should be validated for proper format. Password should meet minimum security requirements (length, complexity). The grade field defaults to ADMIN as SUPER_ADMIN can only be assigned through promotion by existing super administrators.
operations.description:
Register a new administrator account for platform management access.

This endpoint creates a new administrator account in the shopping_mall_admins table with the provided email and password. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts and is validated for proper format. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage.

The administrator grade is automatically set to ADMIN upon registration. SUPER_ADMIN grade can only be assigned through the promotion process managed by existing super administrators via the admin promotion endpoints.

Upon successful registration, the endpoint returns JWT access and refresh tokens in the IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized response, allowing immediate authentication without requiring a separate login call. The access token is used for authenticated requests to administrator endpoints, while the refresh token is used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

This operation is public and does not require authentication. It is typically used during initial platform setup or when new administrators are being onboarded through the registration process.

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and administrator information for authenticated session.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate administrator credentials and issue JWT tokens. Validates email exists in shopping_mall_admins table and password matches the stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison. Checks that the account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Creates a new session record in shopping_mall_admin_sessions table with IP address, href, and referrer metadata from the request. Generates access token with short expiration and refresh token with longer expiration. Returns both tokens along with administrator profile information including grade level.
operations.description:
Authenticate administrator credentials and establish an authenticated session.

This endpoint validates the provided email and password against the shopping_mall_admins table. The email is looked up and the password is verified using bcrypt comparison against the stored password_hash. The account must be active (deleted_at is null) to successfully authenticate.

Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. This session captures connection metadata including the IP address, the full URL (href) where login was initiated, and the HTTP referrer header value. The session has an expiration timestamp that determines when re-authentication is required.

The endpoint returns JWT access and refresh tokens in the IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized response. The access token is used for subsequent authenticated requests to administrator endpoints such as category management, seller approval, and user oversight operations. The refresh token allows obtaining new access tokens without requiring credential re-entry.

The administrator's grade level (ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN) is included in the response, determining which endpoints the administrator can access. SUPER_ADMIN grade grants additional privileges for managing other administrators and approving admin promotion requests.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: JWT tokens and administrator profile for authenticated session.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access token using a valid refresh token. Validates the refresh token against active sessions in shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. Checks that the session has not expired (expired_at is in the future) and the administrator account is still active (deleted_at is null). Generates a new access token with updated expiration. Optionally rotates the refresh token by invalidating the old session and creating a new one. Returns new tokens in IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized format. Used when access token expires but refresh token is still valid.
operations.description:
Refresh JWT access token using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows administrators to obtain a new access token when their current access token has expired, without requiring re-authentication with credentials. The refresh token is validated against active sessions in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table.

The validation process checks that the session exists, has not expired (expired_at is in the future), and the associated administrator account in shopping_mall_admins is still active (deleted_at is null). If the administrator account has been deactivated or deleted, the refresh operation will fail.

Upon successful validation, a new access token is generated with a fresh expiration time. The refresh token may also be rotated depending on security configuration, which involves invalidating the old session and creating a new session record with updated expiration.

The response follows the IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized format, containing both the new access token and refresh token. This operation is essential for maintaining continuous authenticated sessions during extended administrator work periods without requiring frequent credential re-entry.

This endpoint does not require authentication decorator as the refresh token itself serves as the authentication mechanism for this specific operation.

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens for continued authenticated session.

Profile updates are subject to validation checks. The operation will be rejected if the customer account has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null) or if the account is banned by an administrator. Both fields accept updates independently - customers can modify either or both fields in a single request.

When the phone number is updated, the change automatically cascades to all existing shipping address records associated with the customer through the shopping_mall_addresses table, ensuring consistency between the profile and saved addresses. The updated_at timestamp is refreshed to track when the profile was last modified. This operation requires the customer to be authenticated via their session token.

When phone_number changes, cascade the update to all address records associated with this customer by updating the phone_number field in each shopping_mall_addresses record. Retrieve detailed information about a specific authentication session by its unique identifier.

This operation provides session metadata for security auditing and monitoring purposes. The response includes connection details such as the IP address from which the session was initiated, the entry point URL (href), HTTP referrer, session creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. This information enables administrators to track authentication events and investigate security incidents.

Sessions are created when users successfully authenticate and remain valid until expiration or explicit logout. Each session record forms part of an append-only audit trail that cannot be modified after creation. The session expiration enforces security policies requiring periodic re-authentication.

This endpoint is intended for administrative oversight. Regular users view their own session status through account profile endpoints rather than querying sessions by ID. Administrators use this operation to investigate suspicious activity, verify authentication events, or audit user access patterns.

The session ID is a UUID that uniquely identifies the session record across all actor types (customer, seller, administrator, super administrator). The system determines the session's actor type internally based on the session identifier.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the session repository to retrieve session details by UUID identifier. The system must determine which session table to query based on the session ID (customer_sessions, seller_sessions, admin_sessions, or super_admin_sessions). Return session metadata including ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at fields. Do not expose JWT tokens or sensitive authentication credentials in the response. Validate that the requesting user has administrator privileges before returning session details. Handle cases where session ID does not exist by returning 404 Not Found. Include actor type information in the response to indicate which user type owns the session.

responseBody.description: Session details with connection metadata and lifecycle timestamps

parameters.description: Target session's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Search and list password reset requests across all actor types in the platform with advanced filtering and pagination capabilities.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive oversight of password reset activity throughout the shopping mall platform. It aggregates reset requests from customer, seller, administrator, and super administrator accounts, enabling security monitoring and audit trail review.

The endpoint supports filtering by actor type, creation date ranges, expiration status, and token consumption status. Administrators can identify patterns such as multiple reset requests from single accounts, expired unused tokens, or potential security concerns requiring investigation.

Response includes paginated results with reset token metadata, associated actor information, and status indicators. All existing sessions are terminated after successful password change as per security requirements.

Authorization requires admin or superAdmin actor privileges. Customer and seller actors cannot access this endpoint as password reset oversight is a platform administration function.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query all four password reset tables (shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, shopping_mall_admin_password_resets, shopping_mall_super_admin_password_resets) with unified search criteria. Apply filtering by actorType (customer/seller/admin/superAdmin), date ranges (created_at, expires_at), consumption status (consumed_at/used_at null or present), and expiration status. Join with parent actor tables to retrieve email and account information. Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by created_at descending by default. Validate admin/superAdmin authorization before execution. Return unified summary format with actor type indicator for each reset record.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of password reset request summaries with actor information and status indicators

requestBody.description: Search criteria for password reset requests including actor type filtering, date ranges, consumption status, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific password reset request record by its unique identifier.

This operation provides administrators with visibility into password reset requests for audit and security monitoring purposes. The endpoint returns detailed information about a password reset request including when it was created, when it expires, and whether it has been used or consumed.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrator and super administrator actors only. Regular customers and sellers cannot view password reset records through this API. The response excludes sensitive token data (token hash or raw token) for security reasons, showing only metadata about the reset request.

The password reset record indicates its current state: active (not expired and not used), expired (past the expiration timestamp), or consumed (successfully used to reset password). This information helps administrators track password reset activity and identify potential security concerns such as multiple reset requests or unusual patterns.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the appropriate password reset table based on actor context (customer, seller, admin, or super-admin password resets). Verify the requesting user has administrator privileges to access password reset audit records. Return password reset record details including creation timestamp, expiration status, and consumption/usage status without exposing the actual token hash or raw token value. Validate that the resetId exists and return 404 if not found. Include expiration status calculation (expired if expired_at/expires_at < current time). Include usage status (consumed/used if consumed_at/used_at is not null).

responseBody.description: Password reset request information with expiration and usage status

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of email verification records for the authenticated customer.

This operation provides customers visibility into their email verification history, including verification tokens sent during registration or email change requests. Each record displays the token creation timestamp (created_at), expiration time (expires_at), and verification status (verified_at). Customers can track pending verifications, confirm successful email verification, or identify expired tokens.

The endpoint supports pagination for customers with multiple verification attempts. Results are sorted by creation timestamp (created_at) in descending order by default, showing the most recent verification attempts first. For security, token values are never exposed in the response - only metadata about the verification attempts is returned.

Security: Only the customer owner can access their own email verification records. The system automatically filters results to the authenticated customer's shopping_mall_customer_id. Administrators and super administrators can access all customer verification records for platform oversight and audit purposes through separate admin endpoints.

Note: Email verification tokens are system-generated and read-only. Customers cannot create, modify, or delete verification records through this API. New verification tokens are automatically created when customers register or request email changes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table with pagination support. Filter by authenticated customer's ID (shopping_mall_customer_id) for customer actor, or allow admin actors to query all records. Apply sorting by created_at DESC by default. Support optional filtering by verification status (verified vs unverified/expired) through request body. Join with shopping_mall_customers to include customer email in summary response. Return paginated results with IPageIShoppingMallCustomerEmailVerification.ISummary structure containing pagination metadata and array of verification summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of email verification summaries with status and timestamps

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering email verification records

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific email verification token record by its unique identifier.

This operation provides administrative access to email verification records stored in the shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table. Email verification tokens are system-generated credentials sent to customer email addresses during registration or email change requests. Each token contains an expiration timestamp and tracks whether it has been successfully verified.

This endpoint is restricted to administrator actors only, as email verification tokens are sensitive authentication data. Regular customers and sellers should not have direct access to view verification records - they interact with the verification system through registration and verification flows, not by querying verification tokens directly.

The response includes the verification token code, expiration time, verification status (verified_at timestamp if confirmed), and the associated customer account reference. Administrators can use this endpoint for troubleshooting registration issues, investigating failed verification attempts, or auditing the verification system.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table by the verificationId UUID parameter. Return the complete verification record including token, expiration timestamp, verification status (verified_at), and associated customer ID. This operation is for administrative oversight only - email verifications are system-managed authentication tokens, not user-managed resources. Validate that the requesting actor has admin privileges before returning sensitive token data. Handle 404 if verification ID doesn't exist. Do not expose this endpoint to regular customers or sellers as it contains authentication credentials.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of seller accounts on the shopping mall platform.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive search capabilities to manage seller registrations and monitor active sellers. Filters include approval status (PENDING for awaiting review, APPROVED for active sellers, REJECTED for denied applications), suspension status to identify temporarily disabled accounts, and shop name partial matching for quick lookups.

The endpoint supports flexible pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including registration date and shop name. Response includes seller summary information optimized for list displays, showing essential fields like shop name, email, approval status, and suspension state.

Administrators use this endpoint to review pending seller applications, monitor approved sellers, and identify accounts requiring attention such as rejected applications or suspended sellers. This operation is part of the seller management workflow that includes approve, reject, suspend, and unsuspend actions available through dedicated endpoints.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sellers table with pagination and filtering capabilities. Apply search filters on approval_status (PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED), suspended boolean flag, and shop_name partial matching using gin_trgm_ops index. Support sorting by created_at (newest/oldest) and shop_name. Join with shopping_mall_admins table to include approver information when available. Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at is not null). Return cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size. Ensure admin actor authorization check before executing query.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of seller account summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific seller's shop profile.

This operation provides public access to seller shop information including the shop name, description, and logo image URL. The approval status indicates whether the seller is approved to operate on the platform (PENDING, APPROVED, or REJECTED).

All actors (customers, sellers, administrators) can view seller profiles. Sensitive authentication data such as email and password hash are never exposed. The operation validates that the seller account exists and has not been soft-deleted.

Related operations include PATCH /sellers for listing sellers with search filters, and GET /sellers/profile for the authenticated seller's own profile with full details.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId UUID. Return seller profile information including shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, and approval_status. operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrator accounts on the platform.

This operation provides administrative oversight capabilities for browsing and searching administrator accounts. It supports filtering by administrator grade (ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN), email address partial matching, and registration date ranges. The endpoint is designed for super administrators who need to manage the administrator team and for regular administrators who need platform oversight visibility.

The operation excludes soft-deleted (deactivated) administrator accounts from results by default. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and support custom sorting by various fields. The default sort order is by creation date in descending order to show newest administrators first.

Only authenticated administrators (grade: ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN) can access this endpoint. The response includes administrator summary information such as email, grade, and timestamps, optimized for list display purposes. Sensitive authentication data like password hashes are never included in the response.

This endpoint is commonly used together with administrator promotion/demotion operations when super administrators need to review the current administrator roster before making grade changes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admins table with pagination and filtering capabilities. Join with shopping_mall_admin_requests if requester information is needed. Return cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page sizes. Sort by created_at descending by default, with support for custom sorting. Ensure only admin and superAdmin actors can access this endpoint through authentication middleware. Response includes administrator summary information optimized for list displays, excluding sensitive fields like password_hash.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrator account summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator account by identifier.

This operation provides super administrators with complete administrator profile information including email address, privilege grade (ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN), and account timestamps. The endpoint supports administrator oversight and management functions such as grade promotion/demotion and account auditing.

The response includes the administrator's email used for authentication, current privilege grade distinguishing between regular administrators and super administrators, and temporal metadata including creation and last update timestamps. The deleted_at field indicates if the account has been soft-deleted (deactivated).

Access is restricted to super administrators only, as regular administrators cannot view other administrator details. This endpoint complements the administrator list endpoint and is used together with administrator promotion/demotion operations for complete administrator lifecycle management.

Password hashes are never exposed through this endpoint for security reasons. The operation queries the shopping_mall_admins table which stores authenticated administrator identity records with their own authentication flow separate from customers and sellers.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated customer's profile information from the shopping_mall_customers table.

This endpoint returns the customer's profile data including the `nickname` (display name) and `phone_number` fields stored in the shopping_mall_customers table. The profile is automatically created when the customer registers with email and password, and contains required fields that are used throughout the platform.

The `nickname` field appears on reviews written by the customer and is visible to other users and sellers. The `phone_number` field is used for order-related communications such as shipping notifications and delivery coordination. Both fields are required and must contain valid values as defined in the database schema.

This operation requires the customer to be authenticated with a valid session. The endpoint returns only the requesting customer's own profile - customers cannot access other users' profiles through this endpoint. For viewing seller profiles, use the public seller profile endpoints instead.

Related operations include PUT /profile for updating profile information and GET /customers/addresses for retrieving the customer's saved shipping addresses.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_customers table to retrieve the current authenticated customer's profile information. Extract displayName and phoneNumber fields from the customer record. Validate that the customer session is valid and the customer account is active (not banned). Return the profile data as IShoppingMallCustomerProfile. No joins required as profile data is stored directly on the customer record. Handle case where customer has no profile (should not occur as profile is auto-created on registration) by returning appropriate error.
