operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator promotion request, granting the requesting user regular administrator privileges.

This endpoint allows super administrators to approve administrator promotion requests submitted by users. When a request is approved, the requesting user is granted regular administrator (ADMIN grade) access to the platform, enabling them to manage categories, approve seller registrations, view all products and orders, and oversee platform operations.

The approval action transitions the request status from PENDING to APPROVED and records the responding super administrator's ID and response timestamp. A snapshot of the request state is automatically created in the admin_request_snapshots table for audit trail purposes.

Only super administrators can access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot approve or reject admin requests. The request must be in PENDING status; attempting to approve an already processed request (APPROVED or REJECTED) will result in a 409 Conflict error.

Upon successful approval, the system creates a new administrator account for the requesting user with ADMIN grade. The user can then authenticate using the administrator authentication flow.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Approve a pending administrator promotion request. Implementation steps:

1. Verify authenticated user is a super administrator (grade = SUPER_ADMIN)
2. Query shopping_mall_admin_requests by requestId
3. Validate request exists and status is PENDING
4. If not pending (already APPROVED or REJECTED), return 409 Conflict
5. Update request: set status to 'APPROVED', responded_by_super_admin_id to current admin ID, responded_at to current timestamp
6. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_admin_request_snapshots preserving the approved state
7. Grant regular administrator privileges to the requesting user (create shopping_mall_admins record with grade = 'ADMIN')
8. Return the updated admin request with full details

Transaction required: admin request update + snapshot creation + admin account creation must be atomic. If any step fails, rollback all changes.

responseBody.description: Approved administrator promotion request with updated status and response metadata

parameters.description: Target administrator promotion request's ID (UUID format)
parameters.name: requestId

prerequisites.description: Admin request must be created by customer before super administrator can approve it. This operation creates the shopping_mall_admin_requests record with PENDING status that the approve operation references via requestId path parameter.

operations.description:
Reject an administrator promotion request submitted by a customer user.

This endpoint allows super administrators to deny a user's request to become an administrator. When a rejection is processed, the request status transitions from PENDING to REJECTED, and the system records which super administrator made the decision along with the timestamp of the response. The requesting user can view the rejection status and any feedback provided.

Only super administrators have permission to reject admin promotion requests. Regular administrators cannot perform this action. The request must be in PENDING status; attempting to reject an already processed request (APPROVED or REJECTED) will result in an error. Each request can only be reviewed once, ensuring the decision is final.

Upon successful rejection, the system creates an immutable snapshot in the shopping_mall_admin_request_snapshots table to preserve the historical state for audit purposes. The rejected user may submit a new promotion request in the future if they choose to reapply.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Reject an admin promotion request by updating its status to REJECTED. Query the shopping_mall_admin_requests table by requestId. Validate that the requesting actor is a super administrator. Validate that the request status is currently PENDING; if already APPROVED or REJECTED, reject the operation with a conflict error. Update the record: set status to 'REJECTED', set responded_by_super_admin_id to the current super admin's ID, set responded_at to the current timestamp. If a rejection reason is provided in the request body, store it (note: schema may need rejection_reason field addition). Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_admin_request_snapshots table to preserve the historical state before rejection. Return the updated admin request object. Transaction should include both the request update and snapshot creation to ensure audit trail consistency.

responseBody.description: Updated admin promotion request with REJECTED status and response metadata

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the admin promotion request to reject
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Rejection details including optional feedback reason for the applicant

prerequisites.description: Admin promotion request must be created by a customer before a super administrator can reject it. The requestId path parameter references the ID of this created request.

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator grade.

This operation allows super administrators to elevate a regular administrator's privilege level to super administrator. The promotion grants the administrator additional capabilities including managing other administrators (promote/demote) and approving administrator role requests.

The operation validates that the target administrator exists with regular administrator grade (ADMIN) and is not soft-deleted. Only super administrators can execute this operation. Upon successful promotion, the administrator's grade is updated to SUPER_ADMIN and the promotion timestamp is recorded.

This endpoint is part of the administrator hierarchy management system. Related operations include POST /admins/{adminId}/demote for demoting super administrators and GET /admin/promotion-requests for viewing pending promotion requests from users.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_admins table to verify the target administrator exists and has grade ADMIN (regular administrator). Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator (grade SUPER_ADMIN). Update the target administrator's grade to SUPER_ADMIN and record the promotion timestamp. Return the updated administrator record. Reject the request if: target administrator does not exist, target is already a super administrator, target is soft-deleted, or requesting user is not a super administrator. Use database transaction to ensure atomic update.

responseBody.description: Updated administrator information with super administrator grade

parameters.description: Target administrator's ID to promote to super administrator grade
parameters.name: adminId

operations.description:
Demote a super administrator to regular administrator grade.

This endpoint allows super administrators to demote other super administrators from SUPER_ADMIN grade to ADMIN grade. The operation updates the administrator's privilege level, removing their ability to manage other administrators while retaining standard administrative capabilities.

Only super administrators can access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot demote other administrators. Super administrators cannot demote themselves - this restriction ensures at least one super administrator maintains system oversight at all times.

The target administrator must currently hold SUPER_ADMIN grade. Attempting to demote a regular administrator will be rejected. The demotion is recorded with the updated_at timestamp, and the administrator's grade field is changed from SUPER_ADMIN to ADMIN.

This operation is part of the administrator hierarchy management system. After demotion, the affected administrator retains all regular administrator capabilities including seller approval, category management, product oversight, order oversight, and user account management, but loses the ability to promote or demote other administrators.

Related operations include POST /admins/{adminId}/promote for grade elevation and GET /admins for viewing administrator lists (super admin only).
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Implement administrator grade demotion with the following logic:

1. Authorization: Verify the authenticated user is a super administrator (grade = SUPER_ADMIN). Reject if regular administrator or lower.

2. Self-demotion check: Compare the adminId path parameter with the authenticated administrator's ID. If they match, reject the request with 403 Forbidden - super administrators cannot demote themselves.

3. Target validation: Query shopping_mall_admins table for the target administrator by adminId. Verify the target exists and currently has grade = SUPER_ADMIN. If target is not found or is already a regular administrator, reject with 400 Bad Request.

4. Grade update: Update the target administrator's grade field from SUPER_ADMIN to ADMIN. Set updated_at timestamp to current time.

5. Audit trail: The grade change is implicitly recorded through the updated_at timestamp. For enhanced auditability, consider logging the demotion event with actor ID, target ID, and timestamp.

6. Response: Return the updated administrator entity with the new grade value.

7. Error handling:
   - 403: Non-super-admin actor or self-demotion attempt
   - 400: Target not found or already regular administrator
   - 404: Target administrator does not exist

responseBody.description: Updated administrator information with demoted grade

parameters.description: Target administrator's ID to demote from super administrator to regular administrator
parameters.name: adminId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of seller accounts awaiting administrator approval.

This endpoint provides administrators with visibility into pending seller registration requests. Each seller record includes essential information for review decisions: email address for communication, shop name and description to understand the business, and submission timestamp to prioritize older requests.

Only administrator actors can access this endpoint. The operation supports pagination and sorting to handle large volumes of pending requests. Sellers remain in PENDING status until an administrator explicitly approves or rejects their registration through the corresponding approval endpoints.

Related operations include POST /sellers/{sellerId}/approve for approving a seller, POST /sellers/{sellerId}/reject for rejecting with a reason, and GET /sellers/{sellerId} for viewing complete seller details.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_sellers table filtering by approval_status = 'PENDING'. Join with shopping_mall_admins table to include approver information if available. Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) and sorting (default by created_at ascending to show oldest pending requests first). Return seller summary information including id, email, shop_name, shop_description, created_at, and any additional registration details. Ensure only admin actors can access this endpoint through authentication middleware. Handle empty result set by returning pagination with zero data array.

operations.description:
Approve a pending seller registration request, granting the seller full access to create products and manage their shop.

This operation transitions the seller account from PENDING status to APPROVED status. The administrator's ID is recorded in the approved_by_admin_id field for audit purposes. Once approved, the seller can create product listings, manage inventory, process orders, and respond to cancellation and refund requests.

Only administrators with ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN grade can approve seller registrations. The seller must be in PENDING status; attempting to approve an already approved or rejected seller will result in an error. If the seller was previously rejected, the rejection_reason is cleared upon approval.

After successful approval, the seller receives full selling privileges and their products become visible in the marketplace. Related operations include POST /sellers/{sellerId}/reject for rejecting registrations and GET /admin/sellers/pending for viewing pending approval requests.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId. Validate that the seller exists and has approval_status of 'PENDING'. If not in pending status, return an error (already approved or rejected). Update the seller record: set approval_status to 'APPROVED', set approved_by_admin_id to the current admin's ID, clear any rejection_reason if present, and update updated_at timestamp. Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity. Return the updated seller record. Only administrators (grade ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN) can access this endpoint - validate admin session before processing.

operations.description:
Reject a pending seller registration request as an administrator.

This operation allows administrators to reject seller registration applications that are in PENDING status. When rejecting a seller registration, administrators must provide a rejection reason explaining why the application was denied. The rejection reason is stored in the seller record and is visible to the rejected seller.

Upon rejection, the seller's approval_status is changed to REJECTED, the rejection_reason is recorded, and the approving administrator's ID is linked to the seller account. Rejected sellers can view the rejection reason and submit a new registration request after addressing the issues.

Only administrators have access to this endpoint. The seller must be in PENDING status; attempting to reject an already approved or rejected seller will result in an error. This operation is part of the seller approval management workflow described in the platform requirements.
operations.name: reject

Update seller record: set approval_status to 'REJECTED', set rejection_reason to provided value, set approved_by_admin_id to current admin's ID, update updated_at timestamp. Return updated seller object. Error cases: 404 if seller not found, 400 if seller not in PENDING status, 400 if rejection reason missing.

operations.description:
Suspend a seller account, restricting their ability to create or edit products while maintaining access to process existing orders.

This operation is exclusively available to administrators and super administrators. When a seller account is suspended, all products from that seller are immediately hidden from search results and category listings. Customers cannot purchase products from suspended sellers. The suspended seller loses the ability to create new products or edit existing product listings.

However, suspended sellers retain the capability to process existing orders. This includes creating shipments with tracking information, shipping items to customers, and responding to cancellation and refund requests for their order items. This ensures customer orders are not disrupted by the suspension.

The suspension is tracked by setting the suspended boolean field to true on the seller account record. Administrators can later unsuspend the account using the corresponding unsuspend endpoint, which restores product visibility and full seller capabilities.

This operation is part of the seller management authority granted to administrators per the platform governance model. It provides a middle-ground enforcement mechanism between full account approval and permanent banning, allowing administrators to restrict seller activities while maintaining order fulfillment obligations.
operations.name: suspend
operations.specification:
Suspend a seller account by setting the suspended field to true on the shopping_mall_sellers table.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user has admin or superAdmin role
2. Query shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId (UUID)
3. Validate seller exists and is not already suspended
4. Update the suspended field to true and updated_at timestamp
5. Create audit log entry for the suspension action
6. Return 204 No Content on success

Business rules enforced:
- While suspended, all products from this seller are hidden from search results and category listings (enforced at query level in product search endpoints)
- While suspended, products cannot be purchased (enforced at checkout validation)
- While suspended, seller cannot create new products (enforced at product creation endpoint)
- While suspended, seller cannot edit existing products (enforced at product update endpoint)
- While suspended, seller CAN still process existing orders including shipping items (shipment creation endpoint allows suspended sellers)
- While suspended, seller CAN still respond to cancellation and refund requests (cancellation/refund response endpoints allow suspended sellers)

Error scenarios:
- 404 Not Found: Seller ID does not exist
- 400 Bad Request: Seller is already suspended
- 403 Forbidden: Requesting user is not an administrator

parameters.description: Target seller account's ID (UUID format)
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
Unsuspend a previously suspended seller account, restoring their full platform access and product visibility.

This operation is restricted to administrators and super administrators who have the authority to manage seller accounts. When a seller account is unsuspended, all products from that seller become visible again in search results and category listings. The seller regains the ability to create new products and edit existing products.

The seller account must currently be in suspended status for this operation to succeed. If the seller is already active (not suspended), the operation will return an error. This operation does not affect the seller's approval status - it only removes the suspension flag.

After unsuspension, the seller can immediately resume normal operations including product management, inventory updates, and order processing. Existing orders and order history remain unaffected by the suspension/unsuspension process.
operations.name: unsuspend
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_sellers table by the provided sellerId UUID parameter. Validate that the seller exists and is currently in suspended status (suspended = true). If the seller is not found or not suspended, return an appropriate error response.

Update the seller record by setting suspended = false and updated_at = current timestamp. This change immediately restores the seller's product visibility in search and category listings.

Return the complete updated seller profile including shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, approval_status, and the updated suspended flag (now false). The response allows the administrator to confirm the unsuspension was successful.

Ensure this operation is protected by admin/superAdmin authorization middleware. Log the unsuspension action for audit purposes, including which administrator performed the action and when.

responseBody.description: Updated seller profile after unsuspension

parameters.description: Target seller's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
Ban a customer account, preventing the customer from logging in to the platform and accessing any authenticated features.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. When a customer account is banned, the system immediately terminates all active sessions for that customer and prevents any future login attempts using their credentials. The ban action is administrative and used for enforcing platform policies or responding to violations.

All existing orders placed by the banned customer are preserved in the system. The customer's order history remains accessible to administrators and sellers for fulfillment purposes. Past orders continue through their normal status workflow (PAID, SHIPPED, DELIVERED) even after the account is banned.

This operation is idempotent - banning an already-banned customer succeeds without error. To restore customer access, administrators must use the unban endpoint.

Related operations: POST /customers/{customerId}/unban to restore access, GET /admin/customers to view all customer accounts with their ban status.
operations.name: ban
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_customers table to find the customer by the provided customerId UUID. Verify the requesting user has administrator privileges. Update the customer record to set the banned status flag. Terminate all active sessions for the customer by invalidating tokens in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. Preserve all existing orders - do not modify shopping_mall_orders or shopping_mall_order_items. Return success response. Handle edge cases: customer not found (404), customer already banned (can proceed idempotently), requesting user not admin (403).

parameters.description: Target customer's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Restore a banned customer account's login access and platform privileges.

This administrator operation reverses a previous account ban, allowing the customer to log in with their existing credentials and access all platform features. When unbanned, the customer can immediately resume normal platform usage including browsing products, managing their cart, placing orders, and writing reviews.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular customers and sellers cannot unban accounts. The customer's historical data including orders, reviews, wishlist, and addresses remain preserved throughout the ban period and are fully accessible after unbanning.

Existing orders placed before the ban remain in the system and continue through their normal status workflow. The customer's order history is preserved and accessible after account restoration.

Related operations:
- POST /admin/customers/{customerId}/ban - Ban a customer account
- PATCH /admin/customers - List all customer accounts with status filtering
- GET /admin/customers/{customerId} - View specific customer details
operations.name: unban
operations.specification:
This operation unbans a previously banned customer account, restoring their ability to log in and access platform features.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user is an administrator (admin or superAdmin grade)
2. Query shopping_mall_customers table by customerId
3. Validate the customer exists and is currently banned
4. Update the customer's ban status to active (set banned flag to false or remove ban restriction)
5. Return the updated customer information

Business rules:
- Only administrators can execute this operation
- The customer account must exist and be in banned status
- Unbanning immediately restores login capability
- All existing orders and data remain preserved (they were never deleted)
- No notification is sent to the customer automatically

Edge cases:
- If customer is not banned: return error indicating account is already active
- If customer doesn't exist: return 404 not found
- If requester is not admin: return 403 forbidden

Database operations:
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE id = {customerId}
- UPDATE shopping_mall_customers SET [ban_status_field] = false WHERE id = {customerId}

Note: The database schema shows deleted_at for soft deletion, but banning is a separate concern. The ban status field should be verified in the actual schema implementation.

responseBody.description: Updated customer account information after successful unban

parameters.description: Target customer account's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Ban a seller account, preventing the seller from accessing the platform.

This operation allows administrators to ban seller accounts when policy violations or other issues require restricting platform access. When a seller account is banned, the seller cannot log in to the platform using their credentials. The authentication system will reject any login attempts from banned seller accounts.

Banning a seller account does not affect existing orders. All orders placed with the banned seller remain in the system and continue through their normal status workflow. The seller's shop name in past orders is preserved and remains visible to customers who purchased from them. Order items belonging to the banned seller continue through fulfillment, cancellation, and refund processes as normal.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular customers and sellers cannot access this endpoint. Administrators can later unban the seller account using the corresponding unban endpoint, which restores the seller's login access and selling capabilities.

The ban action is immediate and takes effect upon successful completion. Any active sessions for the banned seller should be invalidated by the authentication system.
operations.name: ban
operations.specification:
This operation bans a seller account, preventing the seller from logging into the platform.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user is an administrator (check session/authorization)
2. Query shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId
3. Validate seller exists and is not already banned
4. Update seller account status to banned (set appropriate flag in database)
5. Preserve all existing orders - do not modify order records
6. Return success response

Business rules:
- Banned sellers cannot log in (authentication will reject banned accounts)
- Existing orders remain in system for processing
- Seller's shop name in past orders remains visible
- Order items continue through normal status flow
- Administrator can later unban the account via /sellers/{sellerId}/unban

Edge cases:
- Seller not found: return 404
- Seller already banned: return 400 or 409
- Non-admin user attempts ban: return 403
- Super admin attempting to ban themselves: allowed (no restriction like demotion)

parameters.description: Target seller account's unique identifier (UUID)
parameters.name: sellerId

operations.description:
Restore a banned seller account by clearing the soft deletion timestamp.

This operation allows administrators to unban seller accounts that were previously banned. When a seller is unbanned, their login access is restored and they can resume all selling activities including creating products, managing inventory, and processing orders. The operation clears the deleted_at timestamp on the seller record, effectively reactivating the account.

All existing orders, order items, product snapshots, and seller profile snapshots remain preserved and accessible. The seller's shop name and historical data in past orders continue to be visible to customers and administrators.

This endpoint is restricted to administrator and super administrator roles only. Regular customers and sellers cannot access this operation. If the seller account is not currently banned, the operation will return an error indicating the account is already active.
operations.name: unban
operations.specification: Verify the calling user has admin or superAdmin role. Query shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId. Validate the seller exists and is currently banned (deleted_at is not null). Clear the deleted_at field by setting it to null to restore the account. Update the updated_at timestamp. Preserve all existing orders, order items, and snapshots - these remain unchanged. Return success response. If seller is not banned (deleted_at is null), return appropriate error indicating account is already active.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

instruction:
## E2E Test Strategy

### Test Coverage Requirements

**Authentication & Account Tests**
- Customer signup with valid/invalid email formats
- Customer login with correct/incorrect credentials
- Customer password change (correct current password, wrong current password)
- Customer account deletion (verify orders preserved, reviews show "deleted user")
- Seller signup and approval workflow (pending → approved by admin)
- Seller signup rejection and re-registration
- Seller account deletion restrictions (pending orders, pending requests)
- Seller login restrictions when suspended/banned

**Customer Profile Tests**
- Get customer profile
- Update display name and phone number
- Profile changes after account deletion

**Address Management Tests**
- Add multiple shipping addresses
- Edit existing addresses
- Delete addresses
- Set default address (only one default per customer)
- Address validation (required fields)

**Seller Profile Tests**
- Get seller profile (owner view)
- Update seller profile (verify snapshot created)
- View public seller profile
- View profile snapshots (owner/admin only)
- Profile snapshot preserves shop name, description, logo

**Category Tests**
- List all categories with subcategories
- Admin create category (with/without parent)
- Admin edit category
- Admin delete category (products become uncategorized)
- View products in category
- Category nesting validation (one level only)

**Product Tests**
- Customer search products (pagination, filters: category, price range, in-stock)
- Customer sort products (newest, price asc/desc)
- View product detail (images, variants, seller, reviews, ratings)
- Seller create product (required fields validation)
- Seller edit product (verify snapshot created)
- Seller delete product (restrictions: pending orders, pending requests)
- Admin view all products
- Admin delete any product
- Suspended seller products hidden from search

**Product Image Tests**
- Upload multiple images
- Reorder images (first image is thumbnail)
- Delete images
- Image changes included in product snapshots

**Product Variant Tests**
- Add variant to product (SKU uniqueness)
- Edit variant (verify snapshot created)
- Delete variant (restrictions: pending orders, pending requests)
- Product with no variants shown as "unavailable"
- Variant option values validation

**Inventory Management Tests**
- View inventory history
- Add inventory (restock with positive quantity)
- Subtract inventory (adjustment with negative quantity)
- Current stock calculation (sum of all records)
- Order placement creates negative inventory record
- Cancellation/refund creates positive inventory record
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

**Wishlist Tests**
- Add product to wishlist
- View wishlist (pagination)
- Remove product from wishlist
- Deleted product automatically removed from wishlists
- Duplicate prevention (same product)

**Shopping Cart Tests**
- Add variant to cart
- Adding same variant combines quantities (not separate lines)
- Update item quantity
- Remove item from cart
- Cart total calculation
- Stock warning when quantity > available stock
- Unavailable items marked in cart (deleted/out of stock)
- Out of stock variants cannot be added

**Checkout & Order Tests**
- Checkout review (items, address, total)
- Place order (unavailable items blocked)
- Order creation decreases stock
- Order creation clears cart items
- Order creation saves product/variant/seller snapshots
- Shipping address snapshot preserved
- Order number uniqueness

**Order Management Tests**
- Customer view order history (pagination, newest first)
- Customer view order detail (items, shipments, tracking)
- Seller view order items (filter by status)
- Admin view all orders
- Order status derivation from items (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed)

**Shipping & Tracking Tests**
- Seller create shipment with items
- Items from different sellers cannot be in same shipment
- Tracking information saved
- Shipment items status changed to "shipped"
- Customer view shipment tracking
- Customer confirm delivery (all items in shipment → "delivered")
- Auto-delivery after 14 days from shipping

**Cancellation Request Tests**
- Request cancellation for PAID item only (not SHIPPED/DELIVERED)
- Cancellation request includes reason
- Seller approve cancellation (item → CANCELLED, stock restored)
- Seller reject cancellation
- View cancellation request snapshots
- All items cancelled → order status "cancelled"
- Remaining items continue processing

**Refund Request Tests**
- Request refund for DELIVERED item only
- Refund within 7 days of delivery (reject if older)
- Refund request includes reason
- Seller approve refund (item → REFUNDED, stock restored)
- Seller reject refund
- View refund request snapshots
- All items refunded → order status "refunded"

**Review & Rating Tests**
- Create review for DELIVERED item only
- One review per product per order (prevent duplicates)
- Rating validation (1-5 stars)
- Edit review (verify snapshot created)
- Delete review (soft delete, snapshots preserved)
- View product reviews (pagination, newest first)
- Average rating calculation (excludes deleted reviews)
- Reviews show "deleted user" after account deletion

**Seller Dashboard Tests**
- View dashboard summary (product count, order items count)
- Pending cancellation count
- Pending refund count
- Filter order items by status

**Administrator Tests**
- Submit admin promotion request
- Super admin view pending requests
- Super admin approve/reject promotion
- Promote admin to super admin
- Demote super admin to admin (not self)
- View pending seller approvals
- Approve/reject seller registration (with reason)
- Suspend/unsuspend seller (products hidden when suspended)
- View all customers/sellers
- Ban/unban customers
- Ban/unban sellers
- Force cancel order items
- Force refund order items

**Snapshot Integrity Tests**
- Product edit creates snapshot with all fields + variant snapshots
- Variant edit creates snapshot
- Seller profile edit creates snapshot
- Review edit creates snapshot
- Cancellation/refund request response creates snapshot
- Snapshots are immutable (cannot be modified/deleted)
- Snapshots preserved after original record deletion
- Order items preserve product/variant/seller snapshots at purchase time

**Business Rule Validation Tests**
- Seller deletion: no pending orders (PAID/SHIPPED), no pending requests
- Product deletion: no pending order items, no pending requests
- Variant deletion: no pending order items, no pending requests
- Guest browsing blocked (registration required)
- Suspended seller cannot create/edit products
- Suspended seller can process existing orders
- Banned users cannot login
- Inventory cannot go negative (validation)

### Test Data Setup
- Create test users (customers, sellers, admins, super admins)
- Create test categories and subcategories
- Create test products with variants
- Create test orders in various statuses
- Pre-populate inventory records

### Test Execution Order
1. Authentication & user setup
2. Category management (admin)
3. Seller approval workflow
4. Product management
5. Customer features (wishlist, cart, addresses)
6. Order placement and checkout
7. Shipping and delivery
8. Cancellation and refund workflows
9. Reviews and ratings
10. Administrator oversight functions
11. Snapshot verification
12. Business rule edge cases

scenario.draft: Test that the system returns a 404 Not Found response when an administrator attempts to retrieve a seller profile snapshot with a non-existent or invalid snapshot ID. The admin authenticates successfully, then requests a snapshot using a valid UUID format that does not correspond to any existing snapshot in the system. This verifies the system preserves complete seller profile history for dispute resolution between customers and sellers regarding shop branding and information claims.

scenario.draft: Test the primary success path for browsing all product categories without authentication. This scenario validates that any user (customer, seller, admin, or guest) can retrieve the complete category hierarchy. The test should: (1) Call the endpoint with no request body to retrieve all top-level categories, (2) Verify the response contains pagination metadata (current page, limit, total records, total pages), (3) Verify each category in the data array includes required fields: id, name, created_at, and optional fields: description, parent, (4) Verify all returned categories are root-level (parent is null), (5) Verify soft-deleted categories are excluded from results, (6) Test with different pagination parameters (page=1, limit=10; page=2, limit=20) to ensure pagination works correctly, (7) Verify sorting by created_at descending returns newest categories first. This validates the fundamental category browsing feature that all users rely on for product discovery and navigation.

scenario.draft: Test filtering categories by parent category to retrieve subcategories. This scenario validates the one-level nesting hierarchy business rule. The test should: (1) First, create a top-level category as admin (requires admin authentication and category creation), (2) Create multiple subcategories under the top-level category with different names, (3) Create another top-level category with its own subcategories to test isolation, (4) Call the endpoint with parent_category_id filter set to the first top-level category's ID, (5) Verify the response contains only direct subcategories of the specified parent (not nested sub-subcategories), (6) Verify each subcategory's parent field correctly references the parent category, (7) Test with a non-existent parent_category_id to verify empty results are returned, (8) Verify that subcategories from different parent categories are not mixed in results. This validates the single-level nesting constraint and proper parent-child relationship filtering.

scenario.draft:
Test successful product variant deletion by the owning seller when no blocking conditions exist.

**Setup**:
1. Seller joins and authenticates

5. Seller calls DELETE /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}

**Validation Points**:
- Response returns 204 No Content
- Variant is soft deleted (deleted_at timestamp is set, deleted flag is true)
- Variant no longer appears in product variant listings
- All inventory records for the variant are cascade deleted
- Product remains visible but becomes unavailable if this was the last variant
- Historical order snapshots preserve the variant information

**Edge Cases to Consider**:
- Variant with zero stock quantity
- Variant with multiple inventory records
- Product with multiple variants (deleting one leaves others active)
- Variant that was never added to any cart or order

- Multiple pending order items for the same variant
- Pending order items from different customers

scenario.draft: Test the business rule that prevents duplicate option keys within the same variant. After authenticating as seller, creating a product, creating a variant, and adding an initial option with key='color' and value='Red', the seller attempts to add another option to the same variant with the same key='color' but different value='Blue'. This tests the unique constraint on (shopping_mall_product_variant_id, key) which enforces that each option key must be unique within a variant. The operation should fail with a 409 Conflict error due to the duplicate key, representing a business logic conflict rather than input validation. This validates the business rule that a variant cannot have conflicting option definitions (e.g., cannot have both color=Red and color=Blue as separate options - instead, separate variants should be created for different combinations).

scenario.draft: Test the inventory record query authorization and ownership validation. **Validation Points**:
- Response status is 200 OK
- Data array contains only orders belonging to the authenticated customer
- Order status computation is accurate based on item statuses
- Pagination metadata reflects actual record count
- Default sorting shows newest orders first

Test the primary success path for order creation from a customer's shopping cart.

**Setup Prerequisites:**
1. Register a new customer account via POST /shoppingMall/auth/customer/join
2. Create a seller account and get admin approval
3. Create a product with at least one variant with sufficient stock (e.g., 10 units)
4. Add the product variant to the customer's cart with quantity (e.g., 2 units)
5. Note: Customer must have a pre-existing shipping address (address creation not available via API)

**Test Execution:**
1. Call POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders with a valid addressId belonging to the customer
2. Verify the response contains a complete order object with:
   - Unique order_number generated
   - total_price correctly calculated (quantity × unit_price for all items)
   - shipping_address snapshot matching the provided address
   - items array containing the order item with:
     - Correct quantity and unit_price
     - Status set to 'PAID'
     - productSnapshot capturing product state at order time
     - productVariantSnapshot capturing variant state at order time
     - seller information
   - Empty shipments array (no shipments created yet)

**Post-Condition Validation:**
1. Verify the customer's cart is cleared (GET /shoppingMall/customer/cart returns empty or no items)
2. Verify inventory decreased: Check product variant stock_quantity reduced by order quantity
3. Verify inventory record created: Query inventory records for negative quantity_change with reason 'ORDER'
4. Verify order appears in customer's order history (GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders)
5. Verify order detail is accessible (GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId})

**Business Logic Assertions:**
- Order creation is atomic: all items processed or none
- Snapshots preserve product/variant state at purchase time
- Stock reduction happens immediately upon order creation
- Cart items are removed after successful checkout
- Order items initialized with 'PAID' status ready for seller fulfillment

functions.name: test_api_seller_shipment_retrieve_own_shipment

scenario.draft:
Test that a seller cannot retrieve shipment details for a shipment created by a different seller, enforcing the same-seller authorization constraint.

**Setup:**
1. Customer registers and creates an order with items from two different sellers (Seller A and Seller B)
2. Seller A registers and creates a shipment for their order items
3. Seller B registers separately

**Test Steps:**
1. Seller B attempts to call GET /shoppingMall/seller/shipments/{shipmentId} using Seller A's shipment ID
2. Verify response returns 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden (authorization failure)
3. Verify error message indicates the seller does not have permission to access this shipment

**Business Rule Validation:**
- Different sellers always ship separately (section 87, 199, 325, 459)
- Sellers can only view shipments they created for their own order items (section 203)
- System validates seller authorization by verifying shipment belongs to order containing items from requesting seller's product catalog

**Expected Result:** Seller B is denied access to Seller A's shipment, confirming proper authorization enforcement and data isolation between sellers.

functions.name: test_api_order_item_snapshot_preservation

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can successfully retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within any customer's order on the platform. This scenario validates the admin's platform oversight capability for order management.

**Setup Requirements:**
1. Admin account created and authenticated via /auth/admin/join
2. Customer account with a completed order containing at least one order item
3. Seller account with approved status who listed the product
4. Product with variants that was purchased in the order

**Test Steps:**
1. Admin authenticates via POST /shoppingMall/auth/admin/join
2. Admin calls GET /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId} with valid orderId and itemId from an existing customer order
3. Verify response contains complete order item details including:
   - Order item ID, quantity, unitPrice, and current status (PAID/SHIPPED/DELIVERED/CANCELLED/REFUNDED)
   - Parent order summary (orderNumber, totalPrice, status)
   - Product variant information (skuCode, optionValues, stockQuantity)
   - Historical product snapshot (name, base_price, category at order time)
   - Historical product variant snapshot (sku_code, option_values, price, stock_quantity at order time)
   - Seller information (shop_name, shop_description, approval_status)
   - Timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt)

**Validation Points:**
- Response status is 200 OK
- All snapshot data is present and matches the state at order creation time
- Seller information is current (not snapshot)
- Order item status is correctly reflected
- Authorization works: admin can access order items from any customer/seller combination

**Edge Cases to Cover:**
- Order item in PAID status (awaiting shipment)
- Order item in SHIPPED status (with tracking information)
- Order item in DELIVERED status (confirmed by customer)
- Order item in CANCELLED status (cancelled before shipment)
- Order item in REFUNDED status (refund processed after delivery)

scenario.draft:

- Seller has authority to approve/reject cancellation requests for their order items

- Order item status must be REFUNDED
- Inventory record must exist with reason='REFUND' and positive quantity_change
- Snapshot must be created with immutable state capture
- Seller cannot approve the same refund request again (already responded)

- Error message should indicate refund request already responded to
- Original approval state must remain intact
- No additional snapshots created for failed attempts
- This validates the business rule that only PENDING refund requests can be updated
- Tests idempotency and state transition constraints

scenario.draft:
Test refund request snapshot retrieval when seller has not yet responded to the refund request.

**Setup Prerequisites:**
1. Seller registers and authenticates
2. Customer registers and authenticates
3. Seller creates a product with at least one variant
4. Customer places an order containing the seller's product
5. Seller creates a shipment for the order item
6. Customer confirms delivery of the shipment
7. Customer creates a refund request for the delivered order item (within 7 days of delivery)
8. Seller does NOT respond to the refund request (remains in PENDING status)

**Test Execution:**
Seller calls GET /shoppingMall/seller/refund-requests/{requestId}/snapshots to retrieve the snapshot history for the refund request before responding.

**Validation Points:**
1. Response returns HTTP 200 with paginated snapshot list
2. Pagination metadata shows records count (may be 0 or 1 depending on implementation - snapshot may be created at request creation time or only at response time)
3. If snapshots exist, verify the most recent snapshot shows status as PENDING
4. respondedBySeller field is null (seller has not responded yet)
5. responded_at timestamp is null (no response timestamp)
6. snapshot_at timestamp shows when the snapshot was created
7. customer field contains the customer who submitted the refund request
8. reason field contains the customer's refund reason
9. delivered_at timestamp is populated (required for refund requests)
10. Verify seller can access snapshots for refund requests on their order items even before responding

**Business Logic Verification:**
- Access control allows seller to view refund request snapshots for their order items
- Snapshot state accurately reflects PENDING status before seller response
- System correctly handles viewing snapshots before seller takes action
- No snapshots should exist if implementation only creates snapshots on seller response (verify empty list with proper pagination metadata)

instruction:
## Implementation Requirements

### Authentication & Account Services

**Customer Authentication**
- Signup: Hash password, create user with CUSTOMER role, create customer profile
- Login: Verify credentials, generate JWT token
- Logout: Invalidate token
- Password change: Verify current password, hash new password, update
- Account deletion: Soft delete customer profile, preserve orders, mark reviews as "deleted user"

**Seller Authentication**
- Signup: Create user with SELLER role, PENDING approval status, create seller profile
- Login: Verify credentials AND check approval status (APPROVED only), check not suspended/banned, generate JWT
- Approval status: Return current status with rejection reason if applicable
- Re-registration: Allow rejected sellers to submit new request (reset to PENDING)
- Account deletion: Validate no pending orders (PAID/SHIPPED items), no pending cancellation/refund requests, soft delete products, preserve order history and snapshots

### Customer Profile Service
- Get profile: Return current customer's display name and phone
- Update profile: Validate and update fields

### Address Service
- List addresses: Return all addresses for customer, mark default
- Add address: Validate required fields, set as default if first address
- Edit address: Update fields
- Delete address: Remove address (prevent deleting last address?)
- Set default: Update is_default flag (ensure only one default per customer)

### Seller Profile Service
- Get profile (owner): Return shop name, description, logo
- Update profile: Create snapshot before update, then update fields
- Get public profile: Return shop info without sensitive data
- Get snapshots: Return historical snapshots (owner/admin only)

### Category Service
- List categories: Return tree structure with subcategories
- Get products in category: Filter products by category_id
- Admin create: Validate name/description, handle parent category (one level only)
- Admin edit: Update fields
- Admin delete: Set products' category_id to null

### Product Service
- Search: Full-text search on name, filter by category/price/in-stock, sort options, pagination
- Get detail: Return product with images, variants, seller info, average rating, review count
- Seller create: Validate required fields, link to seller
- Seller edit: Create product snapshot (including variant snapshots), then update
- Seller delete: Validate no pending order items, no pending requests, soft delete product and variants
- Admin list: Return all products with filters
- Admin delete: Force delete any product

### Product Image Service
- Upload: Add image with display_order
- Reorder: Update display_order based on provided order
- Delete: Remove image

### Product Variant Service
- Add: Validate SKU uniqueness, option values format
- Edit: Create variant snapshot, update fields
- Delete: Validate no pending order items, no pending requests

### Inventory Service
- Get history: Return all inventory records for variant
- Add record: Create inventory history entry, current stock = SUM(quantity_change)
- Order placement: Automatically create negative record
- Cancellation/refund: Automatically create positive record

### Wishlist Service
- List: Return paginated wishlist with product details
- Add: Create wishlist entry (prevent duplicates)
- Remove: Delete wishlist entry
- Auto-remove: When product deleted, remove from all wishlists

### Cart Service
- Get cart: Return items with calculated subtotals and total
- Add item: If variant exists, combine quantities; else create new entry
- Update quantity: Validate against stock
- Remove item: Delete cart entry
- Stock warnings: Compare quantity vs available stock
- Availability check: Mark unavailable if variant deleted/out of stock

### Checkout & Order Service
- Review: Validate cart items available, calculate total, get shipping address
- Place order: 
  - Validate all items available
  - Create order record with address snapshot
  - Create order items with product/variant/seller snapshots
  - Decrease stock (create inventory records)
  - Clear cart items
  - Generate unique order number

### Order Service
- Customer list: Paginated, sorted by newest
- Customer detail: Return order with items, shipments, tracking
- Seller list: Filter by seller's products, status filter
- Admin list: Return all orders
- Status calculation: Derive from item statuses

### Shipment Service
- Create: Validate items belong to same seller, create shipment with tracking
- Get tracking: Return shipment details
- Confirm delivery: Update all items to DELIVERED, set delivery_confirmed_at
- Auto-delivery: Cron job to check shipped_at + 14 days

### Cancellation Request Service
- Create: Validate item status is PAID, create request with PENDING status
- Seller list: Return pending requests for seller's items
- Approve: Update request to APPROVED, item to CANCELLED, create positive inventory record
- Reject: Update request to REJECTED
- Snapshots: Create snapshot on each status change
- Admin force cancel: Bypass approval, cancel immediately

### Refund Request Service
- Create: Validate item status is DELIVERED, check within 7 days of delivery
- Seller list: Return pending requests for seller's items
- Approve: Update request to APPROVED, item to REFUNDED, create positive inventory record
- Reject: Update request to REJECTED
- Snapshots: Create snapshot on each status change
- Admin force refund: Bypass approval, refund immediately

### Review Service
- Create: Validate item status is DELIVERED, check no existing review for this product/order
- Edit: Create snapshot before update
- Delete: Soft delete (set deleted flag), preserve snapshots
- List: Return reviews for product, exclude deleted, calculate average rating
- Account deletion: Update user display to "deleted user"

### Seller Dashboard Service
- Get summary: Count products, order items, pending cancellations, pending refunds

### Administrator Service
- Promotion request: Create request with PENDING status
- View requests: Return pending requests (super admin only)
- Approve/reject: Update request status, promote user to ADMIN if approved
- Promote/demote: Update user role (super admin only, cannot demote self)

### Seller Management (Admin)
- View pending: Return sellers with PENDING approval status
- Approve: Update seller to APPROVED
- Reject: Update to REJECTED with reason
- Suspend: Set suspended flag, hide products from search
- Unsuspend: Clear suspended flag

### User Management (Admin)
- View customers/sellers: List with filters
- Ban/unban: Update user banned flag, prevent login when banned

### Snapshot Service
- Product snapshot: Capture all product fields + all variant snapshots
- Variant snapshot: Capture variant fields, link to product snapshot
- Seller profile snapshot: Capture shop name, description, logo
- Review snapshot: Capture rating and content
- Request snapshots: Capture reason and status on each change
- Immutability: Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted

### Business Logic Validators
- Seller deletion: Check order_items WHERE seller_id AND status IN (PAID, SHIPPED), check cancellation/refund requests WHERE status = PENDING
- Product deletion: Check order_items WHERE variant.product_id AND status IN (PAID, SHIPPED), check requests
- Variant deletion: Check order_items WHERE variant_id AND status IN (PAID, SHIPPED), check requests
- Cancellation: Only PAID items
- Refund: Only DELIVERED items within 7 days
- Review: Only DELIVERED items, one per product per order
- Suspended seller: Block product create/edit, allow order processing
- Banned user: Block login

### Security & Authorization
- JWT authentication for all protected endpoints
- Role-based access control (CUSTOMER, SELLER, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN)
- Resource ownership validation (users can only access their own data)
- Admin/super admin checks for administrative endpoints

### Error Handling
- Validation errors (400 Bad Request)
- Authentication errors (401 Unauthorized)
- Authorization errors (403 Forbidden)
- Not found errors (404 Not Found)
- Conflict errors (409 Conflict) for business rule violations
